name: Intra-Muros
description: The walled historic core is Avignon at its most iconic, wrapping the Palais des Papes, Place de l'Horloge, and a maze of stone lanes. Everything is walkable, cafes and shops sit at your door, and the atmosphere is pure Provence, though prices and summer crowds run high.
bestFor: Nomads who want to live in the heart of the action
pros: Best cafes, markets, and monuments nearby
cons: Older buildings can mean noise and few lifts

name: Les Halles Quarter
description: Centered on the Les Halles market and Place Pie inside the walls, this quarter is the city's food and daily-life engine. Mornings bring market shopping and coffee, evenings bring busy terraces around Place des Corps-Saints. It is central, sociable, and slightly more lived-in than the monument core.
bestFor: Cooks, cafe workers, and social nomads
pros: Superb daily market at your doorstep
cons: Can be noisy in the evenings

name: Villeneuve-lès-Avignon
tagline: The quieter side of the Rhone
description: Across the river in the Gard, Villeneuve is a calmer historic town with its own fort, abbey, and gardens, plus fine views back toward the Palais des Papes. It trades the bustle for green space and lower rents while staying a short bus or bike ride from central Avignon.
bestFor: Nomads wanting quiet and value near the center
cons: A short trip from central Avignon

name: La Barthelasse
tagline: River island escape minutes from town
description: The large island in the Rhone is green, flat, and rural, with campsites, walking and cycling paths, and famous views of the city ramparts. A seasonal free ferry links it to the center, making it a peaceful, nature-leaning base that still feels close to everything.
bestFor: Cyclists and nature-first nomads on longer stays
pros: Iconic views of the walled city
cons: Limited services and shops on the island
Ferry is seasonal, so transport can be less convenient
